newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone army says many dead in rebel attack.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone army says many dead in rebel attack.

text.p: Sierra Leonean troops have found nine bodies and believe many more people died when rebels on Friday defied a peace accord to attack a northern town, the army said on Saturday.

"Since the peace accord last November this is the first time the rebels have launched an attack on a town or tried to capture it. They had only carried out small scale attacks before," army spokesman Colonel Abdul Sesay told reporters in the capital Freetown.

Military authorities contacted by telephone in the northern town of Makeni, 160 km (100 miles) from Freetown, said they believed many bodies would be found inside 87 houses razed to the ground in the Friday night attack on Kalangba.
"The rebels fought us off for more than five hours yesterday, soldiers are picking up the corpses of civilians killed and the search continues," one army officer said.
Aid workers said hundreds of rebels were massing in the region, making it impossible to get to people who have been wounded in recent attacks on nearby villages.

A peace accord signed in November between President Ahmed Tejan Kabbah and Foday Sankoh, on behalf of the rebel Revolutionary United Front, was designed to end the war which erupted in 1991 in the impoverished West African state.
The accord has been put in doubt by violent incidents not only by rebels but also by militias who once fought alongside the army.
Aid workers said scores of people had been mutilated in the rebel attack on Kalangba, 24 km (15 miles) from Makeni, and other attacks nearby in the past few days.
"Ten people, some of them with their arms chopped off have reached Makeni government hospital," said one aid worker.
"Many more are trying to make their way to other hospitals in the area. Some have had their arms and some their feet cut off," the source added.
Unidentified gunmen on Tuesday shot and injured a senior U.N. aid official near Makeni and killed his Sierra Leonean driver.

The leadership of the RUF was thrown into confusion in March when one faction, outside Sierra Leone, claimed to have deposed Sankoh. But when officials of the group tried to return home they were held by Sankoh loyalists. Sankoh was last week staying at a hotel in the Nigerian capital Abuja, officials there said.
The war has killed more than 10,000 people.
